notes: Hermes is an IN-PLACE rewind adapter (the claudecode/opencode shape, not codex's fork). /undo soft-deletes the truncated rows (messages.active=0, hermes_state.py:7514) and bumps sessions.rewind_count on the SAME session id — no new row, no parent link. The daemon's only source is the shared SQLite store ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, agent.ProcessOwnedStore); both of its reads filter active=1 (metrics.go foldMessages, watcher.go turnIsDone), so the post-rewind fold is the REWOUND conversation. The rewind writes no message row and does not set ended_at, so watcher.reconcile emits nothing — the row simply dwells in ready, which is why the rewind is asserted as a negative-invariant dwell (rewind_window) rather than a transition. A rewind also never decrements sessions.message_count (only inserts write it), so the watcher's monotonic `grew` comparison cannot swallow the post-rewind turn. session_birth anchors to recording start UNPINNED so a transient proc-<PID> presession cannot steal identity and cascade same_session_as failures; t1_start (the first `working`, which only the real store-keyed session can enter) establishes identity and every later phase pins to it via same_session_as. Turn arcs are driven by an explicit boundary, not an idle heuristic: a user row makes the newest active row non-assistant → Terminal=false → working; the closing assistant row with finish_reason='stop' → Terminal=true → ready. Prompts are deliberately long counting tasks with no tools (scenario asserts tool calls ≤ 0) so each turn spans several 2s watcher polls. NOT asserted here, by design: message counts, cost/token totals (the sessions-row aggregate is not rewound, unlike the conversation fold), and the /undo composer prefill.

text: A hermes session appears in ready (the proc-<PID> presession or the store-keyed id, whichever arrives first — unpinned). Window is generous: the TUI boots 35 tools + 68 skills before the first prompt can land, and the store row is created at turn start.
First prompt → working. Binds identity: the presession never enters working, so the session that does is the store-keyed one every later phase pins to.
First reply completes (assistant row with finish_reason='stop') → back to ready. This is the checkpoint the user will rewind to.
Second prompt → working again on the same session
Second reply completes → back to ready. This is the turn /undo will discard.

Spec: 'Session row reflects the rewound state with state ready'. The user issues /undo 1 -y: Hermes flips the turn-2 rows to active=0 and bumps sessions.rewind_count, inserting nothing and leaving ended_at NULL — so watcher.reconcile emits neither new_session nor activity and the row stays ready. The rewind is asserted only as this negative-invariant dwell.

Spec: 'Subsequent turns start cleanly from the rewound point: ready → working'. The post-rewind prompt drives the SAME session id — Hermes rewinds in place rather than forking, so no new session_id and no parent link ever appear.
Spec: the post-rewind turn completes back to ready on the same session — a clean ready → working → ready arc from the rewound point.
Scenario final state: ready. The session holds ready after the post-rewind turn with no spurious re-entry into working or waiting.
